decision.reason: The successfully patched runner still pins the already-consumed marker and old permit path/id/one-shot id and old native output root. The Host V1 embeds and checks the old permit_id, one_shot_id and marker basename. Reusing either would violate the one-shot guard, while changing only the runner would break host's independent permit/marker checks.
decision.candidate_scope: Only Compile function differed from frozen source in the accepted source repair; its negative test was source-level mutation detection, not a compiler or Windows parameter-binding runtime test.
next_single_integrated_package: Create an exact successor runner and matching Host identity with a fresh, distinct native marker, permit_id, one_shot_id, permit artifact path, and pristine project-contained native output root; retain all previous source/compiler/SCM guards
Retain original consumed marker and its FAIL receipt permanently, no deletion or automatic rerun
Bind SHA256 for successor runner, Host, Engine, Harness, C# compiler and verify a single Windows PS5.1 parse plus focused negative conditions, including compiler argv and successor identity mismatch
Only if integrated source+identity QA PASS, decide ONE new combined compile/isolated-S1-native attempt permit, without separate micro-permits
If eventual compiler or isolated S1 fails, preserve a terminal PASS/FAIL receipt and do not repeat automatically
decision.excluded: No native build/run now; no Broker V3 or Worker V4 rebuild, no SCM mutation, no W01-W12, no P02 opening
